A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DF-R5, DX-LLaVA and PRPO research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across the substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original cross-domain detection results, GPT-4o explanation ratings, and reward and reinforcement-learning ablations in Tables 4–8.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds architecture comparisons, human ratings, perturbation experiments, reasoning-diversity measurements and computational profiling.

M1.justification: The stated optimization objective changes from adding the KL term in v1 Equation 7 to explicitly maximizing the PRPO surrogate minus the KL penalty in v3 Equation 12. This is a limited objective correction; the main architecture, paragraph rewards and PCR algorithms remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish a corresponding implementation change or rerun.

E1.justification: The same five DF-R5 generation domains and face-focused detection task are retained. Appendix B.1 adds evaluation under noise, blur, brightness and contrast changes, JPEG compression and rotation, modestly extending coverage to altered input conditions.

E2.justification: The original detector, MLLM, PPO and GRPO comparator sets are retained. Tables 9–11 add evaluated variants including LLaVA with PRPO, DX-LLaVA with a spatial ViT-L/14 backbone, and supervised PRPO using ground-truth rewards.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include controlled backbone/loss comparisons, reasoning-diversity analysis on 5,000 images, perturbation testing with 100 images per domain and 16 responses per image, and eight human evaluators each rating five images. Computational profiling introduces batch-size and generation-length controls. The newly specified 98%/1%/1% split documents an existing experiment rather than establishing a changed split.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: architecture and auxiliary-loss controls, supervised versus unsupervised rewards, alpha/beta sensitivity, perturbation tests, saliency and representation visualizations, reasoning overlap with Gemini, computational breakdowns and qualitative cases. These investigate component contributions, grounding, teacher imitation and practical behavior beyond v1's existing reward and RL-method ablations.

E5.justification: Appendix E.2 and Table 20 newly report means and standard deviations of iteration time, throughput and latency over the first ten adaptation iterations. This adds runtime variability reporting; detection scores and explanation ratings still lack reported seed-based uncertainty or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: The principal benchmark and GPT-4o rating tables are retained, but Table 3 corrects the language-loss-only model's precision from 70.40 to 98.26. Extensive new results include human averages of 4.630 for PRPO versus 4.220 for Gemini, perturbation accuracy falling from 96.00 to 65.28 under JPEG compression, and architecture, supervised-reward, diversity, sensitivity and timing results. These are newly reported comparisons, not improved scores for the retained benchmarks.

T1.justification: v3 corrects the mathematical optimization specification by explicitly maximizing the PRPO surrogate with a negative KL penalty, replacing v1's positive-KL combined expression. Other equation changes largely expose intermediate notation or clarify embeddings; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the claimed 9% accuracy improvement with a 14.65% average improvement, identified in Section 4.3 as the F1 margin over SIDA. It also removes the claim to be the first reinforcement-learning approach for deepfake detection and explainability. The central dataset, architecture and paragraph-level optimization contributions remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations of backbone representations, label-free versus supervised rewards, reasoning diversity and computational bottlenecks. It newly discusses sparse-artifact majority-vote failures in SiT, limits coverage to face-centric deepfakes, acknowledges dependence on Gemini annotations, and recommends decision-support use. These considerably expand the explanation of mechanisms and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v3 documents paragraph separators, two-layer projector/classifier structures, component parameter counts, full fine-tuning, explicit split ratios and profiling settings. It adds the LLaVA implementation source and changes the stated code/data location from Anogibot/PRPO to tuanrpt/PRPO. These materially expand reproducibility information, although v1's exact ConvNeXT checkpoint reference is removed.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Khan et al. and Nguyen et al. on deepfake detection and Simonyan et al. on saliency, while removing some references, including Foteinopoulou et al. It also withdraws the first-RL novelty claim. The broader related-work framing remains similar; publication and author metadata updates are not new research coverage.

P1.justification: Most existing abstract, introduction, method and results prose remains close to v1. v3 clarifies wording and notation, separates dataset and implementation subsections, adds cross-references, and groups the appendix into thematic sections. Much of the additional prose accompanies new scientific content rather than extensive rewriting of retained material.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint layout to two columns, with substantially resized and repositioned displays. New tables, saliency maps, embedding/confidence plots and qualitative comparison panels substantially expand the visual presentation. Retained material is also relocated: v1's detailed results table becomes Table 17, and its evaluation prompt becomes Figure 13.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation through controlled backbone/loss comparisons, human checks of explanation ratings, and analyses exposing corruption sensitivity, computational costs and failure conditions. These address important evidential gaps in v1; the corrected KL objective and added implementation details also improve reproducibility. The human study is small and does not justify calling GPT-4o unbiased, but this overstatement does not outweigh the substantial gains in evidence and transparency.
